## Current focus

0.1.0 feature-complete on Linux; documentation and release evidence in docs/.

## Roadmap

- [ ] Windows browser worker: CEF sandbox bootstrap (cef_sandbox), Winsock proxy, Windows stdio; then Gate D/E retest.
- [ ] GStreamer runtime bundle (Windows and Linux) with a per-plugin license inventory.
- [ ] Choose a host for runtime bundles and fill the built-in manifest (maintainer decision; nothing is published).
- [ ] Exercise live HLS, shared local assets and private files in a running client; two-player dedicated-server test.

## Decisions

- Geometry: model front faces north (-Z); columns run along facing.getClockWise(); blockstate y = N0/E90/S180/W270
  (block/TvGeometry). Every system uses it, including tests.
- Side boundary enforced by checkSideBoundaries; ClientHooks via DistExecutor is the only common-to-client bridge.
- Session service starts on ServerAboutToStartEvent: spawn chunks load before ServerStartingEvent.
- Screen viewer space: +x right, +y down, +z away from the viewer (Font's convention); layers are tenths of a pixel
  apart and only overlays overlap the picture (client/render/TvRenderer).
- Worker paths are absolute (LocalStore.root): workers run in their own working directory.
- YouTube: native CEF worker (JCEF hardcodes no_sandbox), wrapper served at https://com.otectus.otetv, guarded
  CONNECT proxy; see docs/adr/. Never add --no-sandbox or an autoplay override.
- GameTest coordinates are relative to the structure block; the platform's floor is at y = 1.

## Known issues

- A seek while paused keeps showing the previous frame until play (gst1-java-core has no timed pull for preroll);
  position and captions are correct.
- WebM/MP4 need gst-plugins-good; the bundled demo falls back to its Ogg encode without it.
- Chromium's own background services (component updates, optimization hints) still make requests through the guarded
  proxy; they can only reach public hosts.
